items.context: A filter estimates a quantity that cannot be measured directly. It combines a model of how the quantity changes with measurements that are noisy. When the model is good, the filter trusts it more; when the measurements are precise, it trusts them more. The balance between the two is called the gain. It is computed again at every step, so the filter adapts when conditions change. The same idea guides a robot through a room and a phone through a city.
